title: license payload
description: What a license file of elderlygate/mankit/license/v2 signs (license-file.schema.json's spec.payload, once decoded): its kind, whom it is for, the products and enterprise feature ids it names, the product lines it opens or the day it ends, and the key that signed it (ADR-L1, L2, L4, L6, L8, L9, L10). nw-licenser writes it and mankit's licenses package reads it. It has two kinds where mankit/v1's payload had four: a v1 file is never upgraded, as its signature covers its bytes, and mankit still reads v1's org, product and release-trial for one release (ADR-L8). Open: a newer nw-licenser may add fields here, and an older app accepts them (CT-RULE-4), as several app versions read a license at once (ADR-S15). A field that narrows what a license opens needs a new apiVersion (CT-RULE-1); an added field never narrows it. The signature still covers the payload's bytes exactly, a field the app does not know included. Three rules no schema can say: until is never before issued, id is the file's metadata.id, and lines names exactly the products that products names.

kind.description: Which kind of license it is, so an app knows what it opens (ADR-L8, L9). license: the owner signs it with nw-licenser for a person or an org; it opens the enterprise features it names of the products it names, either until a day or, never ending, in the product lines it names (ADR-L10); one license file per user, read by every app. trial: the trial each product line carries built in, signed once for its line; it opens every enterprise feature of its one app for days from the day its app starts it (ADR-L9).

for.description: The person or org the license names, never a machine, so whoever has the file sees whose it was (ADR-L4); for a trial, which names no one, its product line in words, for example "Acme 1"; never only spaces.

products.description: The enterprise feature ids the license names, per product id, so an app opens a feature only when its own product id names it (ADR-L2). A license names one or more products, each with one or more feature ids; a trial names exactly one, its app, with no feature ids, as it opens every enterprise feature of that app (ADR-L9).

additionalProperties.description: The product's enterprise feature ids, each once, as its feature list names them; never empty, but for a trial's, which is always empty.

lines.description: The product lines the license opens, per product id, each by its number as the constitution's product-lines.yaml names it, so 1 is Designer 1 (V-10). An app opens what the license names only while its own build's line is among them, and a later line needs a new license (ADR-L10). A license that never ends has it, and one with an until never does, as it opens every line while it runs (ADR-L10); a trial always has it, naming its one product's one line, the line it was signed for (ADR-L9).

additionalProperties.description: The product's line numbers, each once.

issued.description: The license's first day, an RFC 3339 date in UTC; it opens nothing before it.

until.description: The license's last day, an RFC 3339 date in UTC, never before issued; after it its features lock again (ADR-L3). A license has it or lines, never both (ADR-L10). For a trial, the day its trial offer ends, not the last day a trial runs: a trial started on that day still runs its days; a trial without it has an offer that never ends (ADR-L9).

days.description: How long each trial a trial license starts runs, in whole days, its first day counted, so every install of the product line's releases gets a trial of the same length (ADR-L9). Only a trial has it, and it always has it. The signing tool writes 14 unless told another length; any length of 1 or more is valid.

allOf.description: A license names one or more products, each with one or more feature ids, has no days, and either runs until a day or names the lines it opens, never both (ADR-L2, L10).
A trial names exactly one product, its app, with no feature ids, the one line it was signed for, and how long its trials run (ADR-L9).

productId.description: A product id, the name the hubman catalog and every answer's source.app give the product (G-PLAN-12).

featureId.description: A product feature id, as the product's feature list names it, which is the one home of its ids (G-STACK-17): lowercase words joined by a hyphen, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters, like events, live-tracing or pdf-export. A license and a switch name a feature by it, so one form holds everywhere. A noun for what the feature is, never a tier or price word such as pro or premium; unique within its product; once released it never changes its meaning and is never reused. Only the form is this schema's to check.
